W2.name: 2-Snap Wire
W2.what: A wire is a road for electricity.
W2.why: It joins pieces together so electricity can travel between them.
W2.how: Snap each end onto a post. Wires can go on top of other pieces too.

W3.name: 3-Snap Wire
W3.why: Use it when two pieces are far apart.
W3.how: Snap each end onto a post.

W4.name: 4-Snap Wire
W4.what: An even longer road for electricity.
W4.how: Snap each end onto a post.

W5.name: 5-Snap Wire
W5.why: It reaches all the way across.
W5.how: Snap each end onto a post.

B1.name: Battery Holder
B1.what: The battery is the pump that pushes electricity around the loop.
B1.why: Nothing works without a push! The battery gives the push.
B1.how: Put 2 AA batteries inside. The red + side is where the push comes OUT. Never join + and − with only wires. That makes it very hot!

S1.name: Slide Switch
S1.what: A switch is a gate on the road.
S1.why: Gate closed (OFF) stops the electricity. Gate open (ON) lets it go.
S1.how: Slide it to ON to turn your project on. Slide to OFF when you are done.

S2.name: Press Switch
S2.what: A button that only works while you hold it down.
S2.why: Great for doorbells and games. Let go and it stops!
S2.how: Press it with your finger. Let go to turn it off.

L1.name: Lamp
L1.why: When electricity goes through it, it gets bright. It can glow dim or bright.
L1.how: Snap it anywhere in the loop. It does not care which way it points.

D1.name: Red LED
D1.what: LED means Light Emitting Diode. It is a tiny red light.
D1.why: An LED uses very little electricity and it only works ONE way.
D1.how: Point the + side toward the battery + side. Always use it with a resistor so it does not break.

D2.name: Green LED
D2.what: A tiny green light. Same as the red LED, just green!
D2.why: Two colors let you make traffic lights and games.
D2.how: Point the + side toward the battery + side. Use with a resistor.

M1.name: Motor + Fan
M1.what: A motor spins when electricity goes through it.
M1.why: Motors make things move: fans, cars, toys.
M1.how: Snap it in, then put the fan on top. Keep fingers and hair away from the spinning fan!

SP.name: Speaker
SP.what: A speaker turns electricity into sound.
SP.why: It is how your project can sing, beep or buzz.
SP.how: Snap it in. It does not care which way it points.

WC.name: Whistle Chip
WC.what: A flat little chip that can beep. It is a baby speaker.
WC.why: It is quieter and smaller than the big speaker.
WC.how: Snap it in like a wire.

R1.name: Resistor 100
R1.what: A resistor slows electricity down, like a speed bump.
R1.why: Some pieces (like LEDs) break if too much electricity rushes in. The resistor protects them.
R1.how: Snap it in the loop next to the LED. Any direction is fine.

R4.name: Resistor 10K
R4.what: A big speed bump. It lets only a tiny trickle through.
R4.why: A transistor needs only a trickle on its B leg to turn on.
R4.how: Snap it in. Any direction is fine.

RV.name: Knob (Variable Resistor)
RV.what: A speed bump you can change by turning the knob.
RV.why: Turn the knob to make lights dimmer or fans slower.
RV.how: It has 3 snaps. Use one END snap and the MIDDLE snap, then turn the knob.

RP.name: Light Sensor (Photoresistor)
RP.what: A speed bump that changes with light. Bright light = small bump. Dark = big bump.
RP.why: It lets your project notice if it is light or dark.
RP.how: Snap it in. Cover it with your hand to make it dark.

C4.name: Capacitor 100uF
C4.what: A tiny bucket that stores electricity.
C4.why: It can keep a light on for a moment after you let go of the switch.
C4.how: Point the + side toward the battery + side.

Q2.name: Transistor (NPN)
Q2.what: A transistor is a magic helper switch with 3 legs: C, B and E.
Q2.why: A tiny trickle into leg B lets a BIG flow go from C to E. It turns a whisper into a shout.
Q2.how: Match the letters C, B and E printed on your piece. B is the control leg.

U1.name: Music Chip
U1.what: A chip with a song inside.
U1.why: Give it power and it plays music through a speaker.
U1.how: Match the + and − to the battery. OUT goes to the speaker.

U2.name: Alarm Chip
U2.what: A chip that makes siren sounds.
U2.why: Give it power and it wails like a fire truck.
U2.how: Match the + and − to the battery. OUT goes to the speaker.

U3.name: Space Chip
U3.what: A chip full of space-battle sounds.
U3.why: Every press makes a new laser or rocket noise.
U3.how: Match the + and − to the battery. OUT goes to the speaker.
